title: A century of dynamo hunting
learning_goal: See the five tracks the community followed for a century (the Earth's record, theory, laboratory dynamos, simulations, reduced models, with a thin data-driven lane), where the three sodium dynamos of ch02 and the supervisors' own papers sit among them, and where MilaDy, the internship and the proposed thesis stand.
takeaway: For a hundred years, theory, laboratory tanks, computer simulations and few-dial models have chased the dynamo together; MilaDy brings machine learning where the tanks, the simulations and the few-dial models meet, and the internship and the proposed thesis bet on machines that generate dynamo fields.
notes: New unit (BRIEF section 10; writers' brief plan/state_of_the_art.md section 2), inserted after ch02 and before ch03 in both cuts: insert_after is the string 'ch02.Q' (BRIEF section 5 form; reviewer 2026-11-08 replaced the object form, which tools/assemble_cut.py cannot use as a module anchor), the last scene of ch02, its question card, in the core and the extended cut alike (the extended running order puts no module between ch02 and ch03). tools/assemble_cut.py places modules only in the extended cut and reads insert_after as a string; for the core cut the foundation engineer can add {'unit': 'chSOA1', 'before': 'ch03'} to EXTRA_UNITS (as ch10q before ch11). NO QUESTION CARD (task instruction for this unit): the plan's chSOA1.Q (which wall and outer-layer properties the simulation campaign must vary; ask C. Nore / Y. Ponty; why: VKS simulations reversed only with a conducting surrounding medium, Bousquet et al. 2026, and wall conditions shift onset, Botez et al. 2026, vacuum versus pseudo-vacuum about 40 % on Rm_c, R:143) is handed to the consistency editor for the question register or ch10q. CONTINUITY: the first line ('Those three tanks...') picks up 02.4 and the cold open's stripes (00.3, thumbnail in SOA1.1); the last line ('Every lane starts from the same race: stretching against smudging') hands over to 03.1, which the consistency editor already changed to open with 'Back to the race' and a chapter card levelFrom L2 (this unit climbs L1 to L2 at SOA1.4). BADGES: CONTEXT everywhere (published history, BRIEF 3.4); SOA1.6 adds a PLANNED chip for the internship and the proposed thesis (T:57). No MEASURED, no PROVED: this unit quotes no E1-E3 number. THE MAP: a new recurring device (motif id to be assigned in styles.md 3.5); its geometry, glyphs, label states and the full pin catalog are in SOA1.1 entry.params (map, catalog), to be copied verbatim into scenes/chSOA1/map.js so the six scenes and chSOA2 draw the same canvas; later scenes list 'present', 'add' (pin id and cue) and 'keep_named'. Every pin carries its reference on screen (line 2 of its label, BRIEF D7). SUPERVISORS (D6): names in text only, on pins and on the SOA1.4 roster box; no photos, no logos, no opinions or intentions; rings say only what each paper showed; the narration never speaks their names (no lexicon entries needed); a grey chip says the summary is independent and not reviewed. Diamonds are the two dynamo papers that declare the MilaDy grant (Bousquet et al. 2026, Botez et al. 2026); Barré and Horii 2026 (off-topic) gets no pin. Bousquet, Nore, Lucor 2025 is NOT a MilaDy paper and is left to chSOA2. WORDING TRAPS AVOIDED (plan/state_of_the_art.md section 6): no 'first' for Lowes and Wilkinson, the 2001 benchmark or DQVU; 'first' only for the 1958 mathematical examples (Rincon) and the first laboratory flips (R:149); DRESDYN 'aims at a dynamo driven by precession alone' (Stefani et al. 2012), no 2026 status; no Larmor title; Glatzmaier and Roberts 1995 by title only; no sodium mass, no Permian dates, no last-reversal date. DRESDYN is not narrated (02.4.s5 already says it aims to join the three); its dashed pin lands silently in SOA1.3. Dropped from the plan to keep the unit near 2.5 min and the map legible: the 2001 benchmark and Iskakov et al. 2007 / Warnecke et al. 2023 pins (low-Pm small-scale dynamos; chSOA2 may use them). SPOKEN NAMES: only place and code names already pinned or requested (Riga, Karlsruhe, VKS, DRESDYN, MilaDy, Reynolds, Pm); Karlsruhe is requested by ch02. FRENCH (BRIEF 9): every sentence has text_fr (same id and cue), a first draft for the French reviewer; 'lane' is rendered 'piste', echoing the author's own question ('quelles pistes la communauté a explorées'); map labels stay in English. PACE: words budgeted with the assembler formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in and tail): after review (2026-11-08): SOA1.1 41 words, SOA1.2 53, SOA1.3 42 (target 20 s), SOA1.4 86, SOA1.5 50, SOA1.6 64 (target 30 s); total 336 words, about 155 s for a target of 159 s (assembler estimate), 127 effective words per minute. External facts were checked on 2026-11-08 (Crossref for every DOI cited, OpenAlex abstracts for Cox 1968, Nore et al. 1997, Rikitake 1958, Meneguzzi et al. 1981, Stefani et al. 2012, Gwirtz et al. 2022, and the arXiv full texts of Rincon 2019 and Stefani et al. 2018); log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/7f944193-0bd4-5776-8423-148e13f15fcf/scratchpad/soa/soa1chk/. UNVERIFIED, kept off screen: Larmor 1919 title and pages, the Glatzmaier-Roberts abstract, DRESDYN's 2026 status. REVIEW 2026-11-08: changelog in script/_review/chSOA1.md.

label_states.active: two lines in a callout next to the pin, panel rgba(16,21,28,0.75), thin chalk leader: line 1 Inter Medium 28 px --fg ('year · words'), line 2 JetBrains Mono 28 px --muted (the reference, no uppercase transform on code names such as SFEMaNS)

map.label_rule: A pin is active from its cue until the next pin's cue in the same scene (at least 2.5 s), the last pin of a scene until the scene's end; then it drops to 'year'. Pins listed in a scene's params.keep_named stay 'named'. Never more than eight pins in 'active' or 'named' state at once; callouts never overlap each other, a lane label or the NOW hairline (Kit.fit plus a bounding-box check at build time). Pins of earlier scenes are present from frame 0 in 'year' state.

On 'stripes-0.15': the 0-5 Myr seafloor strip of 00.3 (params.seafloor, drawn exactly as in 00.3: solid vermillion = normal, near-background = reversed, 360 x 44 px) fades in above lane 1 near x 900, then shrinks into pin E1963 over 0.8 s (T1 callback to the cold open); active label '1963 · seafloor stripes' / 'VINE & MATTHEWS 1963'. Callout placement is computed in setup: two-line active callouts centred on the pin (or in the lane's top row), one-line named labels in the lane's top or bottom row (or just outside the lane when that is free); an active callout hides any named label it covers while it shows; a named label that finds no free place stays a year (a page warning, listed in the build report). Pins carry the year in their callout, so the year under a pin shows only in the 'year' state. No 1.00 to 1.02 push (HTML labels would drift from the SVG).

sentences.text: Lane two, theory.

sentences.text: Nineteen nineteen: a moving, conducting fluid might keep the Sun's field alive.
sentences.text_fr: Mille neuf cent dix-neuf : un fluide conducteur en mouvement pourrait entretenir le champ du Soleil.

sentences.text: Nineteen thirty-three: no flow can sustain a field that is symmetric around an axis.
sentences.text_fr: Mille neuf cent trente-trois : aucun écoulement ne peut entretenir un champ symétrique autour d'un axe.

sentences.text: Nineteen fifty-eight: the first proven examples of flows that can.
sentences.text_fr: Mille neuf cent cinquante-huit : les premiers exemples démontrés d'écoulements qui y parviennent.

sentences.text: In the seventies came simple dynamo flows, later the blueprints of Riga and Karlsruhe.
